subject: Supply Chain & Logistics
title: Roman Roads and Logistics
description: Learn Roman Roads and Logistics in one minute.

hook.text: Rome built 80,000 km of roads—not for tourists, but to move soldiers and supplies fast.

buildup.text: Roman roads were engineering marvels: layered stone, drainage ditches, and uniform width.

discovery.text: They enabled a supply network that fed an empire of 60 million people across three continents.

twist.text: The real innovation wasn't the roads—it was the relay station system that kept messengers moving.

climax.text: When roads crumbled after Rome fell, trade collapsed. Infrastructure is the skeleton of logistics.

punchline.text: All roads led to Rome—and all supplies followed.

quiz.question: Why did Rome build its road network?
options: To move soldiers and supplies efficiently
